A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fine-tuning transfer work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original transfer, multilingual, checkpoint-transferability, further-fine-tuning, and iterative-recycling experiments in Sections 2–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports coding evaluations, generation examples, and cross-architecture transfer experiments.

M1.justification: The main diff-vector addition procedure and iterative Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Appendix B.3 adds a limited cross-architecture adaptation that applies updates only to target layers whose shapes match the source.

E1.justification: V2 adds code generation coverage through HumanEval+, MBPP+, LiveCodeBench, and BigCodeBench. It removes TabMWP and ASDiv from the unseen-task generalization evaluation, retaining GPQADiamond. The original multilingual coverage and training datasets remain.

E2.justification: The new cross-architecture comparisons in Tables 11–12 introduce Llama 2.0 and OLMo 1 base and directly fine-tuned comparison models. The existing main comparator sets and direct-versus-iterative recycling comparison remain; extending the Llama 3 comparisons to coding adds no competing transfer algorithm.

E3.justification: V2 introduces zero-shot, non-CoT, pass@1 evaluation for the four coding benchmarks and additional model configurations for cross-architecture tests. The previously specified checkpoint selections, 30K-step training budget, learning rate, batch size, and retained benchmark protocols are unchanged. Revised scores do not establish that these settings changed.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds paired GSM8K and MATH response examples examining reasoning behavior. Appendix B.3 adds a substantive test of transfer across architectural differences, including weak and negative outcomes. The existing checkpoint-transferability and convergence analyses remain; moving the GPQADiamond matrix into the main text does not constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard errors, or formal significance tests. Table subscripts represent performance differences, not uncertainty, and the learning-curve graphics retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds coding, cross-architecture, and qualitative results and removes TabMWP/ASDiv results. Existing scores also change: Table 6 revises iterative M3 GSM8K accuracy from 67.0 to 63.4, and M5 + delta4 followed by fine-tuning changes from 28.2 to 24.2 on GPQADiamond between v1 Table 13 and v2 Table 5. The original six columns of Table 1 and multilingual Table 2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 already hypothesizes approximately equal fine-tuning updates across versions. V2 Appendix A adds a conditional interpolation derivation, explicit architecture/connectivity assumptions, and task-vector algebra. This provides limited additional mathematical reasoning while assuming update similarity rather than proving it from connectivity.

C1.justification: The five principal contributions remain substantively intact. V2 broadens the abstract's empirical claims to code generation and newly advertises theoretical analysis, while retaining the central claims about inexpensive transfer, multilingual benefits, stronger initialization, and iterative recycling.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning induced step-by-step reasoning and capabilities acquired during post-training. It explicitly qualifies architectural applicability, tentatively attributes weak cross-architecture gains to shape mismatches, and adds an interpretation that iterative recycling avoids error propagation. Existing capability-dependent and Sinhala limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-code link and identifies EvalPlus and the official LiveCodeBench/BigCodeBench evaluation libraries. Existing optimizer, scheduler, sequence length, training budget, and GPU disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the external repository's actual availability.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning through Chat Vector, Re-Adapt, MUSCLE, Trans-LoRA, and RLHF-update extrapolation work, alongside additional connectivity and coding-evaluation references. Section 7 is rewritten around these relationships, while the detailed discussion of Qin et al. is condensed. The added Bandarkar preprint entry duplicates an already cited work rather than introducing distinct research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related work receive substantial rewriting, with additional streamlining throughout the main text. Recycling/backporting explanations are reorganized, the iterative-convergence discussion moves to Appendix F, and the appendix hierarchy is restructured, although the eight main sections remain.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains four coding columns and an average column, and new tables display generation examples and cross-architecture results. The revised GPQADiamond matrix moves from the appendix to main-text Table 5; Algorithm 1 and the iterative-convergence figure move into the appendices. The learning-curve graphics themselves are retained rather than newly generated.

improvement.justification: Coding evaluations, explicit architectural limitations, broader related work, and code-access information add value. However, v2 removes two unseen-task evaluations while retaining broad generalization claims, and some revised scores conflict with retained graphics: Table 4 reports 77.1 for fine-tuned M5 + delta3, while Figure 2 still ends near 78.8. Appendix A also assumes update similarity rather than independently establishing transferability. These benefits and unresolved reporting weaknesses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
